claims.text_en: The unit's two rail stops: BTS Mo Chit (N8), elevated above Phahonyothin Road between Soi Phahon Yothin 18 and 20 in Chatuchak district, opened 5 December 1999 on the Sukhumvit Line, with 5,166,915 passengers in 2021 (13.8025833 N, 100.5538333 E); and MRT Chatuchak Park (BL13), underground beneath the southern part of Chatuchak Park on the west side of Phahonyothin Road, opened 3 July 2004 under its former name 'Mo Chit', with 6,865,636 passengers in 2021. The BTS stop was the Sukhumvit Line's northern terminus until Ha Yaek Lat Phrao opened on 9 August 2019.

geography.notes: Both station boxes sit in the app's merged Mo Chit/Chatuchak Park unit per the merge rule; final polygon membership is the coordinator's check.

temporal_scope.notes: Ridership figures are the newest published on the station pages.

evidence.paraphrase: N8, Sukhumvit Line, opened 5 Dec 1999, above Phahonyothin Rd between Sois 18-20, Chatuchak district, coords 13.8025833/100.5538333, 5,166,915 passengers 2021, northern terminus until 9 Aug 2019.

evidence.paraphrase: Chatuchak Park station code BL13, opened 3 July 2004 (B.E. 2547), formerly named Mo Chit, under the southern area of Chatuchak Park on the west side of Phahonyothin Rd; 6,865,636 passengers in 2021.

claims.text_en: The two stops are one interchange area: OpenStreetMap tags the BTS Mo Chit node (13.80260, 100.55379) and the MRT Chatuchak Park node (13.80296, 100.55328) roughly 70 m apart in straight line (agent-computed), and the English Wikipedia article states the BTS station sits directly above the MRT station with the interchange made at street level outside the paid area. A search-engine summary claiming Chatuchak Park is 'BL12' was tool inference and is contradicted by the body reads: BEM's own site and English Wikipedia give BL12 to Kamphaeng Phet, Thai Wikipedia and OSM give BL13 to Chatuchak Park.

geography.notes: 70 m separation is far inside the 450 m merge threshold; treating this as one merged area unit is consistent with the rule.

temporal_scope.notes: OSM tags can change; coordinator should confirm app station_ids carry N8 and BL13.

limitations: Direct paid-area link between the two systems is not documented in any read source; the transfer is described as street-level.

claims.text_en: The green complex this unit borders consists of three adjoining parks: Chatuchak Park, 0.304 sq km (30.4 ha, ~190 rai), opened 1975 on former State Railway land with a long artificial lake and the MRT line running beneath it; Queen Sirikit Park, 0.22 sq km (~22 ha / 140 rai), a botanical garden established 1992 and formally opened December 1996 with over 2,000 plant species; and Wachirabenchat (Rot Fai) Park, 375 rai (60.0 ha), created 2002 from a State Railway golf course with a roughly 3 km walking/cycling loop. The parks are separated from one another by Kamphaeng Phet 3 Road.

geography.notes: App maps 62.8 ha inside the unit — less than the 112.8 ha component sum, so the polygon appears to clip the complex; which parts fall inside is the coordinator's call.

evidence.paraphrase: Area 0.304 sq km; opened 1975 on SRT land; lake; Chatuchak Park MRT station lies directly under the park; later augmented by Queen Sirikit Park, Wachirabenchat Park and Chak Phupha Su Maha Nathee Park, separated by Kamphang Phet 3 Road.
Queen Sirikit Park 0.22 km2 (140 rai), established 1992, official opening 19 December 1996, 2,000+ species, part of the Chatuchak Park complex.
Wachirabenchat Park 375 rai (60 ha), created 2002, former SRT golf course, ~3 km cycling/walking track, borders Queen Sirikit and Chatuchak parks.

claims.text_en: Agent-computed straight-line distances from the BTS Mo Chit node place the green complex close at hand: Queen Sirikit Park's centroid about 510 m and Chatuchak Park's centroid about 640 m away, both well inside an 800 m catchment, while Wachirabenchat Park's centroid is about 1.1 km to the north (its polygon edge comes nearer; the Overpass radius search still caught the way). The park block therefore reads as genuinely in- or directly adjoining this unit, with Rot Fai the farthest component.

geography.notes: Straight-line from OSM node; no walking-route or duration conversion performed. Polygon clipping decides the final in/out split.

evidence.paraphrase: Centroid distances computed at ~510 m, ~640 m and ~1.12 km; the Rot Fai park way was returned by the 850 m radius search, indicating its southern edge lies within that band.

limitations: Centroid distance understates edge accessibility for large parks; no routing performed.

claims.text_en: Chatuchak Weekend Market, which occupies the blocks north-west of the stations, is described by its visitor site as the largest weekend market in the world: about 35 acres, divided into 26-27 sections, with a paragraph claiming more than 15,000 stalls (the same page's intro says 8,000+ — the site contradicts itself) and more than 200,000 people visiting each weekend. The market office's 2025 figures put permanent stall fees at 1,800 baht/month (green stalls 1,400; plant stalls 900) on land owned by the State Railway of Thailand, for which the BMA pays 169 million baht a year.

geography.notes: The market sits between the Mo Chit and Kamphaeng Phet units; which sections fall inside this unit's polygon is the coordinator's call.

temporal_scope.observed_period: visitor figures current as of site's 2026 copyright
temporal_scope.notes: Renovation (see c06) may move stall counts.

Monthly fees 1,800/1,400/900 baht; BMA runs the market on SRT land and pays 169 million baht a year.

limitations: Stall-count conflict unresolved; visitor figure is the site's own claim without methodology.

claims.text_en: The market is being reorganised: in February 2025 City Hall told 529 stallholders around the clock tower to move out by 30 April 2025 so the zone could be redeveloped as a new tourist-drawing landmark, saying the vending area's walkways had narrowed from 19 m to 9 m. Only about 15 vendors accepted offered alternative stalls (fee waived), 122 were in rent arrears facing contract cancellation, and vendors had petitioned the Prime Minister and the Bangkok governor over the market office's management.

temporal_scope.notes: Post-April-2025 outcome of the redevelopment not found in read sources.

evidence.paraphrase: 529 stallholders ordered out by 30 April; 19 m to 9 m pathway narrowing; new landmark plan; 15 relocations; 122 arrears cases; petition to PM Paetongtarn and Governor Chadchart.
Same deadline, fees and land-payment figures; clock tower zone 'primed to become a new tourist magnet'.

limitations: Vendor-side account available only via a Facebook post surfaced in search (not read); whether the deadline was enforced is unreported in read sources.

claims.text_en: Rents around the unit sit at mid-market for inner-north Bangkok: HipFlat's Chatuchak district averages (October 2026, 4,537 rental listings) are USD 446 for studios, USD 565 for 1-bedrooms and USD 984 for 2-bedrooms, with THB-denominated listings on the page running 16,000-25,000 baht for studios and small 1-beds (e.g. The Saint Residences 16,000; Life Ladprao 21,000-25,000). This is consistent with the app's 16,000/33,000 Chatuchak blend, though the district average is pulled down/north by Lat Phrao-corridor condominiums and no captured listing sat at Mo Chit station itself.

claims.text_en: Day-to-day interchange mechanics: all four exits of MRT Chatuchak Park connect to BTS Mo Chit via the ground level/B1 underpass network (the line runs beneath the park and the BTS sits above Phahonyothin Road), the station has a large park-and-ride lot, and Exit 3 faces the bus stops toward Kamphaeng Phet Road and the Chatuchak bus terminal while Exit 4 faces buses toward Saphan Khwai and the Department of Land Transport.

claims.text_en: The long-distance bus gateway associated with 'Mo Chit' is not in this catchment: Mo Chit 2 (officially Bangkok Bus Terminal, Chatuchak) sits at 999 Kamphaeng Phet 2 Road behind Queen Sirikit Park, roughly 2 km from the BTS/MRT stations per the terminal's article, serving northern and northeastern provinces. In 2025 the Transport Ministry was reported to be weighing consolidation of Bangkok's three long-distance terminals at Krung Thep Aphiwat Central Terminal, which would remove this regional-bus role from the area if it proceeds.

claims.text_en: The unit's rhythm is market-driven: on Saturdays and Sundays the market draws 200,000+ visitors into the blocks between the two stations, while the park complex and residential streets carry the weekdays; Wednesday-Thursday plant-section days and a Friday-night wholesale/night operation extend the surge beyond the pure weekend (the weekday/night schedule appears in secondary guides and should be re-verified against the market office). The station pair's own baseline (5.2M + 6.9M riders in 2021) marks it as one of northern Bangkok's biggest daily nodes.

evidence.paraphrase: More than 200,000 people each weekend; weekend-only market framing.

limitations: Wed/Thu plant days and Friday night hours are snippet-corroborated only (search summaries; no read body stated them) — flagged, not load-bearing.

claims.text_en: Counter-view and gaps: the market's own visitor-review aggregate surfaces complaints worth carrying into copy — limited halal options, variable vendor friendliness, and a maze layout needing comfortable shoes and water — and the 2025 eviction/redevelopment is an open wound with the vendor community. Nothing read supports or refutes a safety-7 for this specific unit (no crime or incident data found), and 'crowd 5' has no unit-specific measurement behind it in any read source; both stay as app values with research finding neither corroboration nor contradiction.

preview.text_en: Two stations in one green pocket: BTS Mo Chit above Phahonyothin, MRT Chatuchak Park beneath the lake-side park, and the weekend market's 15,000 stalls next door — with district rents averaging mid-market and a 2025 redevelopment fight still reshaping the market's clock-tower end.

guide_lead.text_en: Mo Chit is the merged BTS N8 / MRT BL13 interchange on Chatuchak district's southern edge — one node, two systems, a street-level transfer, and the largest weekend market in the world (200,000+ weekend visitors, 35 acres) between them. The green 10 rests on the Chatuchak / Queen Sirikit / Rot Fai park run at the unit's edge (30.4 + ~22 + 60 ha in total, though the app maps only 62.8 ha inside the polygon), and rents track the district's mid-market blend of 16,000-33,000 baht. The frictions are real: an unpaid-area transfer, weekend crowds, a market half-way through a contested renovation, and no unit-specific safety evidence either way.

strengths.text_en: A single merged interchange (BTS N8 + MRT BL13, ~70 m apart) with all four MRT exits wired to the BTS side, a park-and-ride lot, and bus bays off exits 3 and 4.
The Chatuchak / Queen Sirikit park block sits ~0.5-0.6 km from the station node, with 30.4 ha and ~22 ha components verified, plus the market's 200,000-strong weekend economy at the door.

tradeoffs.text_en: The interchange is outside the paid area and the market's weekend surge (200,000+ visitors) transforms the unit's streets twice a week; the 2025 clock-tower eviction of 529 stallholders signals more churn to come.

Rent evidence is district-level only (studio USD 446 / 1BR USD 565 / 2BR USD 984, October 2026) and is dragged by Lat Phrao-corridor condominiums; no station-adjacent listing was captured to confirm the 16,000/33,000 blend at the doorstep.

day_night.text_en: Days split between weekday park-and-commute calm and weekend market gridlock; after dark the unit is quiet by most accounts, with the market's Friday-night wholesale operation the main late activity (schedule snippet-corroborated only).

within_area_variation.text_en: The park-facing western edge (MRT exits 1-2, lake, botanical garden) and the market-facing northern blocks are different worlds from the Phahonyothin commuter strip at the BTS viaduct; Rot Fai Park's bulk lies beyond the catchment's northern reach.

conditional_fit.text_en: Fit for weekend-market regulars, park exercisers and two-line commuters who accept a street-level, separate-ticket transfer.
Poor fit for anyone needing quiet Saturdays, a single-ticket transfer, or guaranteed rent parity with station-adjacent buildings — the rent evidence is district-wide.
